clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock moved only two-tenths of a minute this week, closing at 7:43 p.m., the same reading at which it opened. This near-flat reading concealed a standoff between one of the term's gravest war-powers ruptures and a broad counterweight of judicial rulings, grassroots surveillance reversals, and bipartisan congressional alarm.

grand_total_points.note: The net movement was minimal, reflecting a standoff between severe executive escalation and a comparably strong counterweight of judicial rulings and grassroots resistance.

delta_summary.moral_floor: Severely stressed; restraint and truthfulness suffered extreme breaches during the Iran crisis, while courts and civil society provided the most consistent, though incomplete, counterweight.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The clock's near-flat reading this week does not indicate calm but a rare, unstable balance between an extraordinary expansion of unchecked executive war power and an unusually forceful, if still insufficient, institutional and civic response.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-two traits registered measurable movement this week, spanning executive war powers, judicial independence, voter suppression, crony capitalism, and press freedom.

long_synopsis: Week 64 saw the clock hold nearly still at 7:43 p.m., a stillness masking one of the term's gravest ruptures. The president threatened Iran with civilizational destruction, then unilaterally declared a two-week ceasefire without congressional input, floating a personal financial venture with the same adversary he had just threatened. Cabinet officials offered no resistance. House Republicans twice blocked war-powers votes through procedural refusal, even as more than eighty-five Democrats and some Republicans invoked impeachment and the 25th Amendment. Courts continued ruling against executive overreach while judges faced coordinated intimidation. A federal voter-eligibility purge advanced using an error-prone database. Fifty-three cities canceled surveillance contracts after grassroots pressure, the week's clearest proof that resistance outside Washington still works. Escalation and restraint held each other in a standoff, not an equilibrium.
short_synopsis: A presidential threat of annihilation against Iran, followed by a unilateral ceasefire, exposed the collapse of war-powers checks. Congress raised historic alarm without a vote. Courts resisted; judges faced intimidation. Grassroots pressure rolled back surveillance in dozens of cities.
